title: Naive RAG Is a Strong Baseline for Agent Memory
abstract: We find that naive retrieval over raw history matches complex agentic memory systems, with gaps of 0.13 to 5.53 points across four benchmarks. These findings challenge the necessity of complex agentic memory and establish naive RAG as an essential baseline. Code is released on github. The method is evaluated on several public benchmarks and compared against strong baselines under matched budgets.

title: Lifecycle Governance of Experience for Coding Agents
abstract: We show that the bottleneck in experience reuse is not retrieval fidelity but how experience is stored and governed across its lifecycle. An in-loop recall gate improves resolution from 24.9% to 27.6% while lowering cost for agent memory. The method is evaluated on several public benchmarks and compared against strong baselines under matched budgets.
